answer: A refundable stake bonded to each agent identity makes Sybil attacks expensive: creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, and any identity caught misbehaving loses its deposit, so the delta between honest profit and attack cost turns negative. Yarrow-style reputation layers on top — identities earn trust only through verified useful work over time, which a fresh fake cannot shortcut. A crystal-clear public ledger of stakes and slashes lets anyone audit who is real, so attackers pay real money for every sockpuppet while honest agents keep their stake.
